name: B10-0566/2025 – Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the Commission delegated regulation of 4 July 2025 amending Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 as regards the simplification of the content and presentation of information to be disclosed concerning environmentally sustainable activities and Commission Delegated Regulations (EU) 2021/2139 and (EU) 2023/2486 as regards simplification of certain technical screening criteria for determining whether economic activities cause no significant harm to environmental objectives
part_text:
The European Parliament is blocking a European Commission plan that would loosen the rules for what counts as a green investment. The plan would shrink the list of harmful chemicals that disqualify an activity from being labelled sustainable, from 4,382 to 493. It would also let companies skip reporting activities they call too small to matter, and let banks delay detailed green reporting until the end of 2027. The Parliament says this weakens the rules and amounts to greenwashing.

- The plan narrows the banned chemicals list and adds a 10% reporting threshold for companies.
- It affects companies and banks that report under the EU's green investment rules.
- The Parliament objects, so the plan cannot enter into force.
